$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Cloud SQL. See aws/s3.json for the contract. Feature ids share one namespace with the AWS registry, so they are prefixed gcp.sql.*

gcp.sql.instances.title: Instances (create, list, get, patch, delete, restart, stop/start)
limitations: Instances are RUNNABLE immediately; Vyomi has no provisioning delay (PENDING_CREATE) to model.
Stop/start is simulated by toggling settings.activationPolicy; Vyomi does not actually tear down compute.

gcp.sql.users.title: Users (add, list, change password, delete)
limitations: Cloud IAM authentication type is stored and returned, but Vyomi never checks IAM identity on connect — only the stored password gates access.

gcp.sql.backups.title: Backups (on-demand backupRuns: create, list, delete, restore)
limitations: A backupRun snapshots the control-plane metadata this core manages (databases, users) and instances.restoreBackup replays that snapshot back onto the instance; it does not capture an actual point-in-time copy of table row data (the separate SQL data plane, out of scope for this core).
Automated (scheduled) backups are not taken in the background — only on-demand backupRuns created from the console or API exist.

gcp.sql.operations.title: Operations log (list per-instance and project-wide)
limitations: Every operation completes synchronously and is logged with status DONE; Vyomi has no asynchronous lifecycle to show PENDING/RUNNING operations.

gcp.sql.connections.title: Connections (public/private IP toggle, authorized networks)
limitations: ipv4Enabled and privateNetwork are now enforced on instances.get/list: disabling Public IP removes the PRIMARY entry from ipAddresses (no public address to connect to at all, not a disabled one a client could still dial) and leaving privateNetwork unset means no PRIVATE entry either — the Instances list, instance overview and Connections pages all read this live. authorizedNetworks (the per-IP allow-list) stays unenforced: Vyomi has no real client IP to match against a simulated instance's allow-list, the same honest limit azure_sql_core.py takes for per-IP SQL firewall rules.

gcp.sql.replicas.title: Read replicas
limitations: A read replica is a real instance created with masterInstanceName; it mirrors the primary's databases and users — the control-plane metadata this core manages — synchronously on every write, so Replication lag always reads "0s" rather than modeling real async replication delay. Table row data (the separate SQL data plane) isn't mirrored, and promoting a replica to a standalone primary (instances.promoteReplica) isn't modeled.

A primary instance can't be deleted while it has live replicas (matching the native API), but a replica can still be written to directly — Vyomi doesn't enforce the real engine's read-only restriction on replicas.

gcp.sql.connections-security.title: Connections: Security (SSL/TLS enforcement, client/server certificates)
limitations: Vyomi has no certificate authority and does not negotiate TLS for simulated connections, so it cannot issue client certificates or enforce 'Require SSL/TLS'.

gcp.sql.insights.title: System insights, Query insights and Cloud SQL Studio
limitations: Vyomi collects no CPU/memory/query telemetry for Cloud SQL instances and has no in-console SQL editor backed by the native Admin API, so these dashboards cannot be rendered from real data.

gcp.sql.export-import.title: Export / import (instances.export, instances.import — SQL and CSV files in Cloud Storage)
limitations: Files are written to / read from the simulator's OWN Cloud Storage (a gs:// URI is only parsed, never fetched from Google); a missing bucket or object fails the operation (the Operation carries an error). Each operation completes synchronously.

A SQL export is a plain DDL + INSERT script of the instance's SQL engine (Vyomi's sqlite3/PGlite engine in Nano and for engine-less offline instances, the real Postgres database for offline instances backed by the shared engine container) — not a pg_dump/mysqldump archive; exportContext.databases is recorded but the instance's engine is exported as one database. CSV export requires csvExportOptions.selectQuery and writes no header row.

Offline instances backed by the shared MySQL engine are not supported (the operation fails with that reason); serverless exports, offload, BAK (SQL Server) files and encryption options are not simulated.
